audits.title: 543 Improving the Management of Acute Ureteric Colic in A Multi-Centre District General Hospital: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.standard: BAUS 2018 guidance on acute ureteric colic, including clinic follow-up within 4 weeks
audits.setting: Multi-centre district general hospital, Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust (A&E and urology)
audits.intervention: Teaching sessions for doctors and nurses in A&E and urology.

cycle2.result: Serum calcium 60.4%, CT KUB within 24 hours 97.7%, NSAIDs 67.2% (increases of 20.4%, 0.4% and 5.2%); only 26.4% seen in clinic within 4 weeks, mean wait 41 days.

audits.other_findings: Only 31.3% had acute surgical intervention; a daily emergency theatre slot and computerised clinic booking are recommended.
audits.citation: Desai C, Bruce A, Ehsanullah S, Otite U, Ahmad S. 543 Improving the Management of Acute Ureteric Colic in A Multi-Centre District General Hospital: A Closed-Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.065.

audits.title: WE6.8 An audit to look at the current practice of treating ureteric stones and compare it to NICE/ BAUS guidelines
audits.standard: NICE and BAUS guidelines on ureteric stones (CT within 24 hours)
audits.setting: Chesterfield Royal Hospital, emergency department renal colic presentations

cycle1.result: Average time to CT 16 hours 31 minutes; 6% (3) had definitive inpatient surgery; 62% conservative, 26% stent, 4% nephrostomy.

audits.other_findings: Patients with stents or nephrostomy waited about 7 weeks for definitive treatment.
audits.citation: Minhas A, Moss B. WE6.8 An audit to look at the current practice of treating ureteric stones and compare it to NICE/ BAUS guidelines. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_5). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac248.151.

audits.title: 408 Audit - Diagnostic Pathways in Suspected Renal Colic
audits.standard: BAUS and NICE guidance on ureteric colic

cycle1.result: 335 of 705 had CT KUB within 14 hours; calcium checked in 305 of 636; urate checked in 2.6% (14 of 523); 67 of 200 received NSAIDs as initial analgesia.

audits.citation: Siddique M, Rauf M, Klair A, Mohsin S, Pearce S, Ali D, et al.. 408 Audit - Diagnostic Pathways in Suspected Renal Colic. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac269.018.

audits.title: 1033 Renal Colic Emergency Management - an Audit Cycle
audits.standard: BAUS and NICE renal colic recommendations: CT within 14 hours, NSAIDs, referral criteria
audits.setting: Emergency department, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board, Newport

cycle1.result: NSAIDs prescribed 87%; CT within 14 hours 93%; 100% meeting referral criteria referred; 67% not meeting referral criteria referred.

audits.intervention: Updated NSAID dosing and updated health board renal colic pathway.

cycle2.result: NSAIDs prescribed 50%; CT within 14 hours 100%; 50% not meeting referral criteria referred.

audits.other_findings: Low numbers; all patients having CT KUB suggested as a better identifier for future audits.
audits.citation: Mercer R, Jose M. 1033 Renal Colic Emergency Management - an Audit Cycle. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.173.

audits.title: 380 Audit of the Management of Suspected Ureteric Colic in Barnet Hospital Emergency Department
audits.standard: BAUS/NICE guidelines for suspected ureteric colic
audits.setting: Barnet Hospital emergency department, Royal Free London NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 98% had CT-KUB within 14 hours (mean 4 hours 50 minutes); 52% received analgesia in ED (mean 3 hours 26 minutes from triage); calcium measured in 51% and urate in 4%.

audits.intervention: Education and pathway review; second cycle in progress
audits.other_findings: 22% had an obstructing stone; 75% of these were referred to the stone MDT and 45% had repeat CT-KUB requested.
audits.citation: Dighero I, Ahmad S. 380 Audit of the Management of Suspected Ureteric Colic in Barnet Hospital Emergency Department. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.231.

audits.title: 1167 A Closed Loop Audit to Benchmark Care for Emergency Department Attendances with Renal Colic
audits.standard: NICE quality standards for assessment and management of renal colic (CTKUB timing, NSAID analgesia, time to urological intervention, bone profile/calcium, stone diet advice)
audits.setting: Emergency departments, St Helier and Epsom hospitals (Epsom & St Helier Hospitals, London)

cycle1.result: CTKUB reported within 24 hours 97.9%; NSAIDs 54.5%; surgical intervention within 48 hours 70%; calcium requested 77.9%; dietary/fluid advice 8.7%

audits.intervention: Patient leaflet on stone diet and a renal order-set, plus raising clinician awareness

cycle2.result: CTKUB reported within 24 hours 100%; NSAIDs 71.9%; surgical intervention within 48 hours 100%; calcium requested 94.7%; dietary/fluid advice 39.4%

audits.other_findings: Dietary and lifestyle advice improved but remained low at 39.4%.
audits.citation: Dehbokri A, Mayer C, Ariyanayagam D. 1167 A Closed Loop Audit to Benchmark Care for Emergency Department Attendances with Renal Colic. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.302.

audits.title: 195 Close Loop Retrospective Audit of Acute Ureteric Stone Management: A Comparison with NICE Guidelines and GIRFT
audits.standard: NICE guidelines and GIRFT recommendations for acute ureteric stones
audits.setting: East Surrey Hospital, Surrey and Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Serum calcium checked 47%; dietary advice 17%; stents without clear indication or sepsis 83%; conservative management 65%; urgent treatment within 48 hours 35%.

audits.intervention: Hot primary URS theatre opened and efforts to improve follow-up.

cycle2.result: Serum calcium 66%; dietary advice 72%; stents without clear indication 57%; conservative management 46%; urgent treatment within 48 hours 53%.

audits.other_findings: Lost hot stone clinic follow-ups fell significantly. Staffing and lack of CEPOD support limited primary URS.
audits.citation: Hossain A, Papikinos P. 195 Close Loop Retrospective Audit of Acute Ureteric Stone Management: A Comparison with NICE Guidelines and GIRFT. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.216.

audits.title: SP4.12 An Audit of the investigations of suspected ureteric/kidney calculus in adults in Great Western Hospital, Swindon
audits.standard: NICE NG118: urgent low-dose non-contrast CT for suspected renal colic and serum calcium measurement
audits.setting: A&E and surgical assessment unit, Great Western Hospital, Swindon

cycle1.result: CT within 24 hours in 100%; serum calcium measured in 21%.

audits.intervention: Verbal demonstration, email reminders and notes added to the handover sheet.

cycle2.result: CT within 24 hours in 100%; serum calcium measured in 72%.

audits.citation: Okkeh O, Chikukuza S, Hussain M, Helal A, Emechap E, Hawary A. SP4.12 An Audit of the investigations of suspected ureteric/kidney calculus in adults in Great Western Hospital, Swindon. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_13). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf166.058.
